report_name: Qilin and Akira Ransomware Gangs Claim Flurry of New Victims

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: A Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) group that claimed responsibility for attacks on Calvary Christian College and Insurance Audit Services, Inc. on November 6, 2026. The group is known for targeting critical infrastructure and other sectors.

threat_actors.name: Akira
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that emerged in early 2023, known for its retro-themed leak site. The group claimed a breach against the public accounting firm David L. Wade and Associates, P.C. They are known to exploit VPN vulnerabilities and use tools like Cobalt Strike.

threat_actors.name: INC_RANSOM
threat_actors.description: A Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operation that has been increasingly active in late 2026. The group targeted the major IT service provider Computacenter.

threat_actors.name: n0n
threat_actors.description: A threat actor who claimed responsibility for attacks on retailer Max Fashion and Delta Dental of Missouri.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups like Qilin and Akira for initial access, commonly by exploiting vulnerabilities in public-facing infrastructure such as VPNs and RDP.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: A common initial access vector for ransomware groups like Qilin and Akira.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups to exfiltrate large volumes of sensitive data to attacker-controlled cloud storage before deploying the encryption payload, as part of a double extortion tactic.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The final stage of the attack where the ransomware payload is deployed across the victim's network to encrypt servers and workstations.

attack_patterns.name: Permission Groups Discovery: Domain Groups
attack_patterns.description: Attackers may attempt to find domain-level groups and permission settings, such as using the command 'net group "Domain Admins" /domain'.

malware.name: Qilin Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the Qilin group to encrypt victim networks as part of their double extortion attacks.

malware.name: Akira Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the Akira group to encrypt victim networks as part of their double extortion attacks.

malware.name: INC Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the INC_RANSOM group.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.description: Used by the Akira ransomware gang for persistence and discovery after gaining a foothold in a victim's network.

tools.name: rclone.exe
tools.description: A command-line program to manage files on cloud storage, likely used by ransomware groups for data exfiltration.

identities.name: Calvary Christian College
identities.description: An Australian college listed as a victim on the Qilin ransomware group's data leak site.

identities.name: Insurance Audit Services, Inc.
identities.description: A US-based insurance audit company listed as a victim on the Qilin ransomware group's data leak site.

identities.name: David L. Wade and Associates, P.C.
identities.description: A public accounting firm listed as a victim on the Akira ransomware gang's data leak site.

identities.name: Computacenter
identities.description: A major IT service provider targeted by the INC_RANSOM group.

identities.name: Max Fashion
identities.description: A retail company claimed as a victim by the threat actor 'n0n'.

identities.name: Delta Dental of Missouri
identities.description: A healthcare benefits provider in Missouri claimed as a victim by the threat actor 'n0n'.

infrastructure.name: Ransomware Leak Sites
infrastructure.description: Data leak sites on the dark web used by ransomware gangs like Qilin and Akira to publish stolen victim data as part of their double extortion strategy.

infrastructure.name: Attacker Cloud Storage
infrastructure.description: Cloud storage infrastructure controlled by attackers, used to stage large volumes of sensitive data exfiltrated from victim networks.

indicators.name: Suspicious Reconnaissance Command for Domain Admins
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Reconnaissance Command for Domain Admins
id: 5b6f3a9e-1d2c-4b8a-9f0e-3d4c5e6f7a8b
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of 'net group "Domain Admins" /domain', which is often used by attackers for domain reconnaissance.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
references:
  - https://www.breachsense.com/breaches/
tags:
  - attack.t1069.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'net group "Domain Admins" /domain'
      - 'net group Domain Admins /domain'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of a command to enumerate members of the 'Domain Admins' group, a common reconnaissance technique for attackers.

indicators.name: Rclone Execution Detected
indicators.pattern:
title: Rclone Execution Detected
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-2c1d-0e9f8a7b6c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of rclone.exe, a tool that can be abused by threat actors for data exfiltration to cloud storage services.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
references:
  - https://www.breachsense.com/breaches/
tags:
  - attack.t1567.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rclone.exe'
    OriginalFileName: 'rclone.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of rclone.exe, a legitimate tool often abused by ransomware groups for data exfiltration.

indicators.name: DNS Query for .onion Domain
indicators.pattern:
title: DNS Query for .onion Domain
id: 1d2e3f4a-5b6c-4d7e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries for .onion domains, which may indicate communication with Tor hidden services, often used for C2 or accessing leak sites.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
references:
  - https://www.breachsense.com/breaches/
tags:
  - attack.t1090
level: low
logsource:
  category: dns_query
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith: '.onion'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries for .onion domains, which could indicate attempts to access ransomware leak sites or other dark web infrastructure.

indicators.name: Rclone File Execution

  category: file_event
  product: windows

  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\rclone.exe'
  condition: selection
